Question 2

Why is it wrong to attack a nested conditional conclusion (like "if I go to the moon, I need space shoes") by asking "what if you don't go to the moon?"

Correct!

The author only claims the rule holds in the world where the sufficient condition is activated. Negating the sufficient condition sidesteps that claim entirely instead of disproving it. The rule just sits there, dormant and unaffected.
